description: The plot titled “Hidden State Mean” shows mean absolute hidden-state values across model layers for three conditions (before gating, after gating, and a baseline). The x-axis is labeled “Layer” on a linear scale, spanning layers 0 through 23 with tick labels shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Abs Mean” on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 5 with integer tick marks. Three lines are shown: a blue dashed line (legend: “hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71”) that starts near about 0.05 at layer 0, stays around roughly 0.2–0.5 through the mid layers, rises to around ~0.9 by about layer 19–20, then increases sharply to about ~2.6 around layer 21–22 and ends near ~4.4 at layer 23; an orange dotted line (legend: “hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05”) that begins near 0 at layer 0 and gradually increases with small fluctuations, reaching roughly ~0.1 by the final layers; and a green solid line (legend: “hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04”) that also begins near 0 at layer 0 and slowly increases across layers, ending around ~0.1 near layer 23.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the mean absolute values of hidden states across different layers, comparing values before and after gating, as well as against a baseline. The x-axis is labeled 'Layer' with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 24, and the y-axis is labeled 'Abs Mean' with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 5. The blue dashed line represents the 'hidden state mean before gate,' which shows a steady increase across layers, peaking at approximately 5.5 in layer 24. The orange dotted line represents the 'hidden state mean after gate,' which remains relatively stable across layers, with a slight decline after layer 15. The green solid line represents the 'hidden state mean of baseline,' which remains consistently below the post-gating values across all layers. The legend in the top left provides a clear description of the three lines.
